title: EV brand E-Went eyes mass market, to test sodium-ion batteries from Dec
description:
Kolkata-based Saraogi E-Ventures, which markets electric two-wheelers under the E-Went brand, sees significant growth opportunities in India's price-sensitive markets, particularly in the sub-Rs 1 lakh segment, while exploring sodium-ion battery technology as an alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries, its founder and CEO Umang Kumar Saraogi said.
The company plans to begin trials of sodium-ion battery-powered scooters around December, deploying some vehicles for testing. The technology is being explored for its potential safety advantages over conventional lithium-ion batteries, although its relatively lower energy density makes the battery packs bulkier, Saraogi said.
"It is supposed to be safer. We expect to conduct trials here starting in December and deploy some vehicles with these batteries. The economics and convenience have to be evaluated before we can deploy them in our new product launches. Currently, most of the models use lithium-ion technology," he told PTI.
